rationale: The negative half of the arrow question, and the fixture whose stated belief was WRONG until R was run against it. R desugars both rightward forms to `<-`(value, name) at parse time, so a name on the LEFT of `->` is not a declaration -- it is a runtime error, `invalid (do_set) left-hand side to assignment` -- and publishing a symbol for `name_on_left -> 6` invents a binding R refuses to make. An earlier revision of the analyzer read whichever side happened to be an identifier and did exactly that. tree-sitter-r does NOT desugar, which is why the two sides have to be distinguished from the operator field. The comment in this file used to assert that `function() 1 -> valid_fn_right` is a declaration. IT IS NOT, and the oracle that "verified" it was the wrong instrument: R's own parser puts the rightward assignment INSIDE the function body -- `eval(parse(text="function() 1 -> x"), new.env())` leaves `ls()` empty on R 4.6.1 -- and tree-sitter-r agrees, giving `function_definition > binary_operator op="->"`. Parenthesising the value is what makes it a declaration, and `(function() 1) -> valid_fn_right_parens` is pinned as one. The three forbids and the three pins are the same assertion from both directions: the OPERATOR decides which side binds, and nothing else about the line does.
